entries.speaker: Phillip Padgett

entries.text: I'm here to help you finish.
entries.speaker: Ken Naciamento

entries.text: I can't figure out your motive.
entries.speaker: Phillip Padgett

entries.text: You imagine me so perfectly in every way-- so perfectly that you bring me to life. Why did you choose me?
entries.speaker: Ken Naciamento

entries.text: I needed a perfect crime. And she's a doctor. She'd be horrified by what you do.
entries.speaker: Phillip Padgett

entries.text: I'm horrified. I just want to know why I do it.
entries.speaker: Ken Naciamento

entries.text: So I could meet her.
entries.speaker: Phillip Padgett

entries.text: That's not a reason. It's an excuse.
entries.speaker: Ken Naciamento

entries.text: Anything?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: No, he's just sitting there. Staring.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Now what is this?
entries.speaker: Ken Naciamento

entries.text: A big mistake. I misjudged her character, her interest in me.
entries.speaker: Phillip Padgett

entries.text: Now we're on to something.
entries.speaker: Ken Naciamento

entries.text: She's only trying to get his attention, but doesn't know it.
entries.speaker: Phillip Padgett

entries.text: Mm-hmm. The old unconscious at work.
entries.speaker: Ken Naciamento

entries.text: I wanted to love her.
entries.speaker: Phillip Padgett

entries.text: No wonder you can't finish this book, Padgett. Why do I want their hearts?
entries.speaker: Ken Naciamento

entries.text: You tell me. Why do you do it?
entries.speaker: Phillip Padgett

entries.text: I'm your character. You tell me. My reason is your reason.
entries.speaker: Ken Naciamento

entries.text: I want to feel love.
entries.speaker: Phillip Padgett

entries.text: Mmm-- no. No. You had it right up to there. You were a tool of the truth. And when it finally arrives-- when I arrive, you don't want to see it.
entries.speaker: Ken Naciamento

entries.text: But what is the truth?
entries.speaker: Phillip Padgett

entries.text: Man imagines that he too... Can open up his heart and expose the burning passion-- the flames of charity. Like the creator himself, but... This is not in his power.
entries.speaker: Ken Naciamento

entries.text: But I have love in my heart.
entries.speaker: Phillip Padgett

entries.text: Yes, as a thief has riches, a usurer, money. You have it! But man's only power-- only true power... Is to destroy it.
entries.speaker: Ken Naciamento

entries.text: Then what's the end of my story?
entries.speaker: Phillip Padgett

entries.text: There can only be one true ending... If it is to be perfect.
entries.speaker: Ken Naciamento

entries.text: She dies?
entries.speaker: Phillip Padgett

entries.text: See? It almost writes itself.
entries.speaker: Ken Naciamento

entries.text: What's he up to now?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: He just started typing again.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Now what? Anything?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: [ door closes ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: Padgett! Freeze. Step away from the incinerator.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: [ gasps ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: What do you think you're doing?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Destroying my book.
entries.speaker: Phillip Padgett

entries.text: Destroying evidence, you mean. Let me see what you wrote.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: I'll tell you. He kills her.
entries.speaker: Phillip Padgett

entries.text: [ screaming ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: [ screaming ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: You came down here to give these instructions to your accomplice?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: No, he told me how it ends.
entries.speaker: Phillip Padgett

entries.text: When?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: In my apartment.
entries.speaker: Phillip Padgett

entries.text: You were alone up there.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: [ gunshot ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: [ grunting ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: [ gasps ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: [ panting ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: [ sobbing ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: A story can have only one true ending. Even as the stranger felt compelled to commit his final words to paper, he did it knowing they must never be read. To see the sum of his work was to see inside his own emptiness-- the heart of a destroyer, not a creator. And yet reflected back upon him, at last he could see his own ending. And in this final act of destruction... A chance to give what he could not receive.
entries.speaker: Phillip Padgett
